- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.3), model overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with downward trend.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days to correct for momentum decay.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion toward historical range (e.g., 70–75) after a spike, model often overreacts; apply downward correction in 2–4 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the period when sentiment is volatile; apply 2–5% downward bias for first 7–10 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.8, 0.27, 0.8), model often misaligns with sentiment cycles; use sentiment-weighted smoothing to dampen overfitting.
